entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Wang Dayuan, courtesy name Huanzhang, was a Chinese traveller from Jiangxi in the 14th century known for his two major ship voyages to India and Southeast Asia.\n\nBorn in unknown year, Wang Dayuan embarked on his first voyage in 1340, visiting the ports of Calicut and Galle in present-day India.\n\n
Wang Dayuan's second voyage, undertaken between 1351 and 1354, took him to the Southeast Asian kingdoms of Srivijaya and Majapahit.\n\n
Wang Dayuan's journeys not only expanded Chinese trade networks but also facilitated the exchange of ideas, cultures, and technologies between East Asia and the Indian Ocean world.\n

Wang Dayuan's legacy as a pioneering Chinese traveller has endured for centuries, inspiring generations of scholars and explorers to explore the ancient world.\n

The Chinese traveller's writings, though incomplete, offer a unique window into the lives of medieval Chinese traders, diplomats, and adventurers, revealing the intricate web of relationships between China, India, and Southeast Asia during the 14th century.\n

Wang Dayuan's voyages are a testament to the dynamism and resilience of the maritime trade networks of the medieval world, which played a crucial role in shaping global history.\n

The records of Wang Dayuan's journeys have been preserved in the Song Shi, a historical text compiled during the Ming dynasty, providing valuable insights into the history of Chinese maritime trade and cultural exchange during the 14th century.
